key_insight: Interpretability is only one component of a model’s broader semantics; using a formal notion of model semantics from the philosophy of science lets us systematically analyse and disambiguate what ‘interpretability’ means in biomedical deep learning models.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a formal, principled framework to define and evaluate interpretability in deep learning—particularly in high-stakes biomedical applications—by separating interpretability from other semantic aspects of models.
method: Adopt a formal, philosophy-of-science notion of model semantics to characterize what models represent and how representations map to domain phenomena.
Define a framework that distinguishes interpretability from other semantic properties (e.g., causal content, representational fidelity) and prescribes analytic checks.
Illustrate the framework with concrete biomedical examples showing how different semantic aspects affect trust, validation, and use.
impact: Provides practitioners a clearer vocabulary and analytic toolkit to set realistic interpretability goals, design appropriate validation procedures, and improve transparency and trust in biomedical AI systems.
visual_elements: Concept diagram: layered model semantics with ‘interpretability’ highlighted as one subset among other semantic components (causal, predictive, representational).
Flowchart: data → model → semantic mappings → interpretability checks, showing evaluation points for biomedical workflows.
Case-study panel: side-by-side examples from biomedicine (e.g., diagnostic imaging vs. molecular models) illustrating differing semantic demands and interpretability outcomes.
Evaluation matrix: checklist/table mapping semantic property → practical tests/metrics → implications for deployment and regulation.
paper_title: Interpretability and implicit model semantics in biomedicine and deep learning
paper_authors: Jonathan Warrell, Michael Gancz, Hussein Mohsen, Prashant Emani, Mark Gerstein
